subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw add a core automatic final-output sensitive-data sanitization boundary, and what default scope/config should it use relative to existing log/tool/transcript redaction, SecretRefs, plugin hooks, and channel delivery?
rationale: The security goal is valid, but default-on behavior, false positives, config shape, plugin ownership, and user-visible output mutation require maintainer/security intent before implementation.

options.title: Design a core boundary
options.body: Add a security-reviewed core sanitizer that reuses existing redaction infrastructure and starts with a documented, tested scope across final replies and adjacent sinks.

options.title: Use plugin hooks first
options.body: Keep core policy minimal and add only missing extension points so an official or community sanitizer plugin owns detection and output behavior.

options.title: Document current limits
options.body: Decline broad final-output filtering for now and document reliance on SecretRefs, log/tool redaction, local models, and explicit skills/plugins.

recommendation.title: Design a core boundary
recommendation.body: Add a security-reviewed core sanitizer that reuses existing redaction infrastructure and starts with a documented, tested scope across final replies and adjacent sinks.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently owned the adjacent SecretRef egress and exact-value redaction hardening, and this decision is a security-boundary extension of that work.
